title: MCP Python SDK v2: FastMCP Is Now MCPServer
caption:
I pinned mcp<2 and went back to bed.

MCP Python SDK v2 landed July 28. FastMCP is now MCPServer, and the old import path wasn't deprecated, it was deleted. Anything without an upper bound in pyproject.toml crashes with ModuleNotFoundError. The protocol went stateless in the same release: no initialize handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id.

Honestly the rename is the right call. I just wish it hadn't shipped the same week as the spec.

Pinned or ported?

slides.headline: FastMCP is gone
slides.sub: MCP Python SDK v2 shipped July 28. The class every Python MCP server imports is now MCPServer, and the old path was removed, not deprecated.

slides.title: One import, renamed
slides.sub: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP is now from mcp.server import MCPServer. Unpinned installs crash with ModuleNotFoundError.

slides.title: Sessions are gone
slides.sub: The protocol is stateless. No initialize handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id header. Any request can land on any instance.

slides.title: Pin it or port it
slides.sub: Not ready? mcp>=1.28,<2 holds you on v1.x. But that branch is critical bug fixes and security patches only.

slides.headline: Check your pyproject
slides.sub: and I'll send the migration notes
